concepts.question: Is there a homogeneous white opacity filling part of the lung, dense enough that the vessels running through that region can no longer be traced?

absent.text: vessels can be followed from the hilum out to the periphery against dark lung, with no region of uniform added whiteness

patchy.text: one or more ill-defined white areas, each under about a quarter of a lung, obscuring the margins of the vessels inside them

confluent.text: one uniform white region obscuring vessel and airway margins across most of a lobe or a whole half of the chest

concepts.question: Is there a hazy, veil-like increase in whiteness of the lung through which the vessel and airway margins can still be seen?

absent.text: the lung is uniformly dark between the vessels, with no veil of added grey over any zone

mild.text: a faint veil of grey over part of one lung through which vessel margins stay traceable, only less sharp

marked.text: a dense veil over most of both lungs, vessels only just discernible through it but still not wholly obscured

concepts.question: How prominent are the fine linear, net-like markings of the lung, over and above the normal smoothly branching vessels?

normal.text: only smoothly branching vessels that taper outwards and fade before reaching the chest wall

increased.text: thin lines persist out to the chest wall, including short horizontal lines at the bases meeting the ribs at right angles

coarse_reticular.text: innumerable small linear opacities cross one another into a visible net, coarser and more angular than any vessel

concepts.question: If any increased whiteness is present, how strongly is it concentrated in the lower zones near the diaphragm rather than spread evenly or set in the upper zones?

absent.text: any added whiteness is spread evenly between upper and lower zones, or sits mainly above the hila

mild.text: the lower zones are visibly whiter than the upper zones, but the same change still reaches above the hila

marked.text: the whiteness is confined below the hila and the upper zones are as dark as normal lung

concepts.question: Is the sharp angle where the diaphragm meets the chest wall blunted or filled in, with an upward-curving upper edge against the chest wall?

absent.text: on both sides the diaphragm meets the chest wall in a sharp acute point

mild.text: the angle is rounded off and filled in, but the whole curve of the diaphragm dome is still visible

marked.text: whiteness fills the angle and climbs the chest wall with a concave upper edge, hiding part of the dome

concepts.question: Is there a band or plaque of soft-tissue whiteness lying along the inner chest wall or capping a lung apex, following the surface of the lung rather than a vessel?

absent.text: lung markings reach the ribs, with only rib shadows along the inner chest wall and no band of soft-tissue grey

mild.text: a thin grey band, or a cap over one lung apex, follows the chest wall and is narrower than one rib

marked.text: a rind of soft-tissue whiteness wider than a rib follows the chest wall over several rib spaces

concepts.question: How wide is the heart shadow compared with the widest inner diameter of the chest, a ratio of about one half being the usual upper limit?

narrow.text: the heart shadow spans under about a third of the widest inner chest diameter and looks tall and vertical

normal.text: the heart shadow spans between about a third and one half of the widest inner chest diameter

wide.text: the heart shadow spans more than half of the widest inner chest diameter

concepts.question: Is there a discrete, roughly round, sharply outlined white lesion inside the lung, and if so is it small (under about one fifth the width of one lung, roughly 3 cm) or larger?

absent.text: no rounded, sharply outlined white spot stands out from the branching pattern of the vessels

small.text: a rounded opacity up to about a fifth of one hemithorax wide (3 cm); at 1 cm it is near 6 pixels here and unreliable

large.text: a rounded opacity wider than about a fifth of one hemithorax, that is, over 3 cm across

concepts.question: Is a thin white line visible running parallel to the chest wall, with completely blank lung beyond it and no vessel markings reaching out to the ribs?

absent.text: vessel markings run out to the ribs all round, with no thin white line running parallel to the chest wall

present.text: a thin white line parallels the chest wall with blank, vessel-free lung between it and the ribs

concepts.question: How inflated do the lungs look: short with high domed diaphragms, normal, or tall and dark with low flattened diaphragms and widely spaced ribs?

reduced.text: the diaphragm domes sit high and steeply curved, the rib spaces are narrowed and the lungs look short

normal.text: gently domed diaphragms near the tenth posterior rib, with evenly and moderately spread rib spaces

increased.text: diaphragm outlines flat or concave upward, rib spaces widened, dark lung reaching below the tenth posterior rib

concepts.question: Is the trachea or the heart shadow off the midline, and if so is it pulled towards the whiter (more opaque) half of the chest or pushed away from it?

towards_whiter_side.text: the tracheal air column and heart shadow are displaced into the whiter half of the chest, the darker half looking larger

none.text: the tracheal air column runs down the middle of the frame and the heart shadow sits centred between the lungs

away_from_whiter_side.text: the tracheal air column and heart shadow are pushed into the darker half, away from the whiter one

concepts.question: Is there an abnormal rounded structure projected behind the heart or above the diaphragm that contains gas or a gas-fluid level and distorts the diaphragm outline?

absent.text: the diaphragm outline is a smooth unbroken curve with no gas pocket above it behind the heart

present.text: a rounded gas-containing pocket, sometimes with a flat fluid level, projects above the diaphragm behind the heart
